summary: The main article describes a rhodium-catalyzed direct hydrocarboxylation of styrenes using CO2 and H2, facilitated by visible light. It includes an optimization table for reaction conditions, a substrate scope figure, and detailed mechanistic and computational studies.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Carboxylation of ole fi nic compounds using CO2 and H2. a Target transformation: catalytic direct hydrocarboxylation of ole fi ns using CO2 and H2, a 100% atom economical reaction. b Previous strategy: rhodium-catalysed reverse watergas shift equilibrium (rWGS)/hydroxycarbonylation. c Our strategy: visible-lightfacilitated reductive carboxylation using H2 as the terminal reductant. d This work: visible-light-enabled direct hydrocarboxylation with CO2 and H2. LED, lightemitting diode.
items.description: This figure outlines the conceptual framework of the research, comparing the target 100% atom-economical hydrocarboxylation with previous high-temperature strategies and the current visible-light-enabled approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions and control experiments
items.description: This table details the screening of rhodium catalysts, ligands, and control experiments to optimize the yield of the hydrocarboxylation product 2a versus the hydrogenation byproduct 3a.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Scope of substrates. Reaction conditions: 1 or 5 (50 μ mol), CO2/H2 (2:1, 1 atm, closed), [Rh(C2H4)(DavePhos)](OTf) (2.0 μ mol), DavePhos (4.0 μ mol), [Ru(bpy)3](PF6)2 (1.0 μ mol), DMA (1.0 mL), blue LEDs (425 nm), room temperature, 5 h.
items.description: This figure displays the chemical structures and yields for various styrene derivatives and an acrylate substrate subjected to the optimized hydrocarboxylation conditions.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Experimental mechanistic studies. a Proposed mechanism. b Hydrogenolysis of rhodium acetate 7 with H2. c Reactivity of benzylrhodium 9 .
items.description: This figure illustrates the proposed catalytic cycle and experimental evidence for key intermediates, including the hydrogenolysis of rhodium carboxylates and the reactivity of benzylrhodium species.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Computational studies. Free-energy diagram of a hydrocarboxylation and b hydrogenation of 1a with RhH(Davephos) 7 ( CP1 ) as a catalyst computed at the M06/SDD(Rh)&6-311+ G(d,p)(C, H, N, O, P), SMD(DMA)//LANL2DZ(Rh)&6-31 G(d,p)(C, H, N, O, P) level.
items.description: This figure presents the DFT-calculated free-energy profiles for both the desired hydrocarboxylation and the competing hydrogenation pathways.
